title: THE MOURNER WHO REMEMBERED TOMORROW
deck: A being of slow glass mourns, every evening, a fire in Karrow's furnace quarter that has not happened yet, and the glassmakers want it dragged out of town. Illuminara has four days to learn what it remembers, to find out whether a remembered tomorrow can be made wrong, and to let the people who work the fire be the ones who put it out.
shape: Seven scenes across five days: a lament in a lamplit square, a night of slow questions, a draw from a master's apron, a test the witness could have failed, a night of small changes and untouched controls that shows which memories refuse to move, a hammer on a stack the master has paid to open, and an evening in which the mourner writes its own terms.

scenes.title: The Lament
paragraphs: *Karrow, the Square of Lamps · evening, day one*

Karrow made glass the way other towns made weather: all day, everywhere, and without anyone thanking it. When Illuminara came down the hill road the chimneys of the furnace quarter had burned their smoke to gold, and in the middle of the Square of Lamps something tall and pale sat on the fountain rim, singing to nobody.

It was a being of slow glass, taller than a doorway, folded in the middle the way a sitting person folds. Light went into it at the speed of honey and came out a moment late, so that every lamp in the square seemed to reach it after it had passed. A woman in a grey shawl sat beside it on the rim, knitting. She did not look up.

**Orem**  
It was the fourth night. The stack sang, and then the street was orange. I remember the sound a spoon makes in an empty pot. I remember the needles lying in the ash.

**Edda**  
Evening, Orem. Three more days of it, is it?

**Orem**  
Three, and the fourth night. Edda. I am sorry that I remember you this way.

**Edda**  
I'm sat right here. Mind your tenses.

A man had come up behind Illuminara, broad in the shoulders, with a master's burn scars on both forearms and two apprentices holding a handcart like a pair of nervous pallbearers. Inge Voss, who had run the Karrow annealing guild for twenty-two years, looked at the being and not at the stranger.

**Inge Voss**  
A year of this I could stand. Last week it learned numbers. The great run is lit on the fourth night, and my glassmakers have started asking each other what hour the fire is. That has to stop. The cart goes to the quarry road tonight.

**Illuminara**  
Master Voss. What does it say that you can't answer?

**Inge Voss**  
That's the whole trouble. If its tomorrow is a fact, there is nothing for me to do about it, and I'll not stop a year's work for a fact. If it is not a fact, then why is a stranger screaming in my square?
It was a good objection, and Illuminara noticed she was glad of it. A town that had only sneered at the being would have been easier to argue with and harder to help.

**Illuminara**  
Give me until the lamps are out. If I come back with nothing but a speech, take the cart.

**Inge Voss**  
Until the lamps are out. Then the cart.

scenes.title: The Minute Before
paragraphs: *Karrow, the Square of Lamps · night, day one*

She did not begin with the fire. *Slowly,* she told herself. *It is only slow because nobody has been willing to wait.* She sat down on the fountain rim on the side away from Edda, with the being's long shadow across her knees, and asked what it was like.

**Orem**  
Nobody has asked. ... It is like standing at the far shore of a lake. The water is the world. I see it from the other side. What is ahead of you is behind me. Do you understand?

**Illuminara**  
Not yet. I'd like to.

It took an hour for the being to tell her, each sentence arriving whole and a little late, and she let every one finish. Somewhere in the second hour she realised she was no longer waiting for the answer. She was listening to the sound of a mind that had been alone with the same grief for a year, and the grief had a shape and a rhythm, like a tide.

**Illuminara**  
Tell me the minute before the street is orange. Then the minute before that.

**Orem**  
The stack sings. A low note, hollow. A spoon in an empty pot. ... Before that, blue. Blue at the foot of the stack, where there is no blue in daylight. Before that, the smell in the third hall. Lard-oil, burning. I do not know why the smell is there. Before that, the lamp on the sluice bridge, green. And the drum of the stack is cold, and Edda is sitting in the third hall with her flask, and she says: Well, that's not right.

**Edda**  
That's what I'd say, mind. That's exactly what I'd say.

**Illuminara**  
Orem. Is what you remember a verdict, or a map?
The being went still. In the lamplight the glass of its face clouded slowly, as when a thought passes through deep water.

**Orem**  
I do not know. I have never been told I could be wrong. ... If you make me wrong, I will lose the ash. I will lose her face in it. I have kept it so carefully.

**Edda**  
Don't be soft. You'll keep the face I've got.
Illuminara did not tell it that it would not hurt. She put her hand flat on the cold rim between them, where the stone was warm from the day, and left it there.

**Illuminara**  
I'd like to be the reason you're wrong. I won't change anything of yours. I'll only change things in the world, and ask you what you find. May I?

**Orem**  
Yes. ... Yes. I would like to be wrong more than I would like to keep it.

scenes.title: Three Slips
paragraphs: *Karrow, the master's yard · morning, day two*
Voss had come with her arms folded and brought a cap full of paper. She emptied it onto the anvil, and it was clear she had been awake as long as Illuminara had.

**Inge Voss**  
I'll not have my yard convinced by a stranger who agrees with everything the creature says. Three things a person could change in an hour. I wrote them, the new state of each as well. You haven't seen them. You'll do whichever I draw. It will be told nothing, and Edda will sit on it like a hen until you're done.

**Illuminara**  
Good. If I'd picked, you could say Orem read it off my face.

**Inge Voss**  
I could say it still. Draw.
She drew one slip from the cap, folded it in four, and gave it to Illuminara without letting go of the corner for a moment. Illuminara read it once.
*Replace the chimney glass of the third lamp on the sluice bridge with amber.*
The other two slips, Voss kept: one to turn the bridge gate outward, one to hang a bell on the east post. She kept them in her apron, where they could not be accused.

**Illuminara**  
Master Voss, one more thing. If it comes out wrong, it will say so.

**Inge Voss**  
It's a lamp, woman. It will be right or it won't.

By noon the amber glass was in its iron cage on the sluice bridge, and for the first time in a year the old lamp over the water burned the colour of tea. Illuminara walked back through the market and did not look at the square.

scenes.title: What It Said
paragraphs: *Karrow, the Square of Lamps · dusk, day two*

They asked it at lamplighting, with Voss standing three paces back and the mason Dov Haldane beside her. Dov was a lean man in a leather apron who had been called as a witness because he trusted nothing and had never once lied about a wall.

**Inge Voss**  
Orem. The fourth night. Tell me the lamp on the sluice bridge. Then the gate. Then the bell.

**Orem**  
The lamp is amber. ... It was green, yesterday. I remember the green very well, because I have looked at it for a year. It is amber now, and I do not know why, and I did not choose this. The gate is as before. The bell is as before.
Nobody spoke. Edda put down her knitting.

**Orem**  
I do not remember the fire any differently. The stack sings. The street is orange. But the lamp is amber. Something is wrong with my tomorrow, and it is exactly where she has been.
It was not triumph in Illuminara. It was closer to holding out a hand for a very long time and feeling someone, at last, close their fingers on it.

**Dov Haldane**  
One in three that it picked the right slip by luck, and amber's a one-in-six colour, so call it one in eighteen. I've seen better luck at a fair. A trick with a good conscience.

**Inge Voss**  
Fair, Dov. One lamp proves it can see a lamp. It doesn't prove the stack.

**Illuminara**  
Agreed. A lamp is the cheap part of the memory. Master Voss, I'd like to change more cheap parts tonight, and let your apprentice draw the slips. The expensive parts are what I'm after.

**Dov Haldane**  
Then do it so it can fail. Fifteen changes. Voss writes each target and its new state tonight, before the first question, and I seal the list. Six things we leave alone and ask about anyway, mixed in, so it can't just say changed to everything. It misses two, or calls an untouched thing changed, and the map's a story.

**Inge Voss**  
And the cart goes. And hear this: the pot is at heat and the pour is on the clock. I will not hold it for you or for a fire. You open my stack, you do it with the sand running.

**Illuminara**  
Agreed, both. If I change fifteen small things and it follows me on all of them, and the six I leave alone stay as they were, then the lamp and the gate and the bell were never what the fire was made of. And whatever it can't be made to change—

**Dov Haldane**  
—is what the fire was made of. Aye. That's a map of the bits that matter.
He said it without warmth and with such obvious professional interest that Voss looked at him sharply. Then she sent for her apprentice.

scenes.title: What Would Not Move
paragraphs: *Karrow, the Square of Lamps · night, day two*

By midnight it was fifteen for fifteen, and six for six on the things nobody had touched. The apprentice, Wil, had drawn the slips out of Dov's sealed cap with his tongue between his teeth: a blue ribbon on the fountain, a loaf left on the sluice step, the gate on the east post painted white. Each time Orem had named the change as soon as it was asked, without looking, and each time the change had been exactly where Voss's ink said it was. Voss had stopped saying one in eighteen.

**Dov Haldane**  
The baker's sign.

**Orem**  
As before. ... You are trying to catch me, Master Haldane.

**Dov Haldane**  
Aye.
He sounded a little disappointed. What did not move was the other thing. Edda had counted it for them on her fingers.

**Edda**  
The stack sings. The blue at its foot. The oil in the third hall. Me, in the third hall, saying it's not right. Four. It won't shift an inch for all your ribbons.

**Illuminara**  
Because the ribbons never touched the cause. Orem, the note of the stack. How far up, and which side?

**Orem**  
On the side the wind does not come from. Two spans up. Where the third hall's flue enters the great stack. The note is not in the brick. It is behind it.

**Dov Haldane**  
Behind. That's a hollow liner. Hollow behind the lining brick, with the cold stack still looking handsome. And where the third hall's flue joins the stack, there's an iron collar old Haakon put in after the flood. Iron and brick, heating at two speeds. It cracks the lining where nobody sees, and a crack in a lining draws air the wrong way, and the draught goes backwards into a hall with an oil lamp in it.

**Edda**  
Backward draught. That's the lard smell. That's why it smells of the kitchen.

Illuminara went to the stack at one in the morning and laid both palms on it. The load lay through the brick as it had lain for ninety years, perfectly ordinary, perfectly quiet. She could feel the weight of the collar and nothing else. A crack that only opens in the heat has no force in it when the wall is cold, and she stood with her hands on the stone for a long moment, annoyed at herself, then not annoyed.

**Illuminara**  
I can't find it. Not cold. I can tell you where to look, now, because the lake told me. I can't tell you it's there.

**Dov Haldane**  
I can. With a rod. At first light.

scenes.title: The Rod
paragraphs: *Karrow, the great stack · dawn, day three*
Voss insisted on tapping it herself, and before she took the rod she said it to the whole yard, so that nobody could say afterwards what she had meant.

**Inge Voss**  
If it rings, the cart takes the stranger and her lamp, and the pour goes as written. If it's hollow, I bank the pot and we open the stack.

**Dov Haldane**  
Bank it? That's a night's best metal gone to cord, Inge, and six hundredweight of coal. And you'll not have the lehr drawing till the castable sets.

**Inge Voss**  
Aye. And you'll not put a hammer to a wall with a pot at full heat on the other side of it. That's your rule, Dov. Who pays is mine.

She took Dov's steel rod, a thin thing with a rubber foot, and went up the scaffold on the lee side with the whole yard watching from below, and the rod rang on sound brick as bright as a bell. Two spans up she stopped. She tapped again.
It did not ring. It made a sound like a spoon in an empty pot.
For a time she did not move. When she came down her face had gone the grey of old slag.

**Inge Voss**  
It's hollow. A hand's width behind the face, all round the collar. I've fired that stack for twenty-two years.

**Dov Haldane**  
So have I. Not once did either of us hit it cold.

Voss turned and sent a boy running to the pot-house. By the time the scaffold was up, its fires had sunk to a red sleep, and the glass in the pot was beginning to stiffen and dull, a night's best metal slipping away.

**Inge Voss**  
I said I'd not hold the pour for a fire. I'm not holding it for a fire. I'm holding it for a mason. I'll reline it, Dov. Because the mason says it's bad. Not because a stranger and a lamp said so. Understood?

**Dov Haldane**  
Same wall, Inge.

**Inge Voss**  
Same wall.

Dov's crew cut out the collar by afternoon. Illuminara took its weight on the scaffold, three tons of old iron lifted a finger's breadth off the brick, so that the masons could knock out the cracked liner without a hammer-blow shaking it down. She held it for six minutes, and Edda timed her. She set it down when Dov said now and not before, and walked down the scaffold with her forearms shaking, because it was Dov's wall.

They worked through the night of the third day and into the fourth with floodlamps and fast-setting castable, and at noon the pot-house was woken on fresh coal. Voss paid every mason double and never said why.

scenes.title: Edda's Needles
paragraphs: *Karrow, the Square of Lamps · evening, day five*

The great run was lit on the fourth night, with the pour at dusk and the lehr drawing sweet and steady, and the eleventh bell came and went over a quarter of low roofs and quiet stacks. Nobody cheered. Karrow stood in its doorways listening to the wind, and went to bed one by one, as people do when a thing has not happened.

On the fifth evening Illuminara came back to the fountain. Edda was in her place with her needles, and the being sat on the rim with its face turned toward the amber lamp on the sluice bridge, which was still the only lamp in the quarter the colour of tea.

**Orem**  
I have been asked what I remember of the fourth night. ... It is quiet. The stack has no song. You are asleep, Edda, with your boots on, and the lamp is amber. I do not have the ash any more. I have been trying to keep it. I find I cannot.

**Edda**  
Well, there's a thing.

**Orem**  
I did not know that I would be so sorry to lose it. I have kept it a year. It was the last place I had her face.
Illuminara felt that, and let it be felt. She did not say that it was a small price. The being had given up a year's grief, and a year was not small.

**Illuminara**  
I can't promise her face is anywhere but the ash. But she's eight inches from your elbow. Would you like to look at her? You may say no.

**Orem**  
... Yes.
The long head turned. The lamplight arrived late and settled over the grey shawl, the hands, the pulled-tight wool.

**Orem**  
She is knitting. A sleeve. She has dropped a stitch and is pretending she has not. ... She is humming a note that is flat.

**Edda**  
It is not flat.

**Orem**  
It is a little flat. I would like to hear it tomorrow.

Inge Voss came across the square as the lamps took the last of the light, a broad shape with her sleeves rolled and a ledger under one arm. She did not look at Illuminara. She did not apologise, and nobody in Karrow had expected her to. She opened the ledger on the fountain rim beside the being and turned it so that it could read.

**Inge Voss**  
The guild has voted. From the next firing, every stack is tapped cold before it's lit, and the tapping is entered in the book. And there's a line here with nothing written on it. We've no name for what you are to this quarter, and I'll not give you one. You write it.

**Orem**  
... I would like to be asked, not told. I will say what I remember to whoever asks me, and I will say I remember, not that it will be. Nobody acts on it until a mason has put a rod to it. And I may be silent. Some of what I remember is Edda's.

**Dov Haldane**  
That's my rule, creature. Gladly.

**Inge Voss**  
Written. And from us?

**Orem**  
I do not know what is usual. ... The stool at the fountain, which is already mine. The amber lamp left as it is. And that a person writes in the book every time I am wrong. I would like to be wrong in writing.

**Inge Voss**  
The lamp stays. Wil keeps the book, he's the hand for it. Tea's still optional.

**Orem**  
I do not drink tea.

**Inge Voss**  
Optional, I said.
She went back across the square and did not turn round. Edda pushed her needles together and began a new row.

**Orem**  
Edda. I remember something. It is the first frost. In three weeks. It is a long way off, and it is only frost. I am telling you, not the guild. ... I do not know if it is true.

**Edda**  
Then we'll go and see, won't we.

critic_line: The slow-glass mourner's warning becomes a testable, freely shared rescue rather than a prophecy imposed from above: Dov supplies falsifiable controls, Voss pays to open the dangerous stack, Orem chooses reciprocal terms for its gift, and the furnace workers retain the authority that prevents the fire.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1; two genuine isolated model judgments; exact equal 50/50 arithmetic mean.
shared_strengths: Strong premise, an emotionally real mourner, and dialogue-driven problem solving where the test design pays off in the hollow-liner reveal. The humane ending works. The middle's procedural detail (odds, sealed slips, masonry) may slow some readers, and the name-heavy cast is a mild barrier.

The slow-glass mourner is an instantly memorable idea, and the dialogue turns a careful causal investigation into humane drama about consent, grief, and revisability. The middle grows slightly procedural as tests accumulate, but each test deepens character and earns the tender, unsentimental ending.

By midnight it was fifteen for fifteen, and six for six on the things nobody had touched.

translation_sl.title: ŽALOVALEC, KI SE JE SPOMINJAL JUTRI
translation_sl.deck: Bitje iz počasnega stekla vsak večer žaluje za požarom v Karrowovi četrti peči, ki se še ni zgodil, steklarji pa ga hočejo odvleči iz mesta. Illuminara ima štiri dni, da izve, česa se spominja, ugotovi, ali je spominjani jutri mogoče spremeniti, in poskrbi, da bodo ogenj pogasili ljudje, ki z njim delajo.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v petih dneh: žalostinka na trgu v soju svetilk, noč počasnih vprašanj, žreb iz mojstričinega predpasnika, preizkus, pri katerem bi se priča lahko zmotila, noč majhnih sprememb in nedotaknjenih kontrol, ki pokaže, kateri spomini se nočejo premakniti, palica ob dimniku, za katerega odprtje je plačala mojstrica, in večer, v katerem žalovalec zapiše lastne pogoje.

scenes.title: Žalostinka
paragraphs: *Karrow, Trg svetilk · večer, prvi dan*

Karrow je izdeloval steklo tako, kot so druga mesta ustvarjala vreme: ves dan, povsod in ne da bi se mu kdo zahvalil. Ko je Illuminara prišla po cesti navzdol, so dimniki četrti peči svoj dim ožgali do zlate barve, sredi Trga svetilk pa je nekaj visokega in bledega sedelo na robu vodnjaka ter pelo nikomur.

Bilo je bitje iz počasnega stekla, višje od podboja, na sredini prepognjeno tako, kot se prepogne sedeč človek. Svetloba je vanj vstopala s hitrostjo medu in izstopala trenutek pozneje, zato se je zdelo, da ga vsaka svetilka na trgu doseže šele, ko je že minila. Ob njem je na robu sedela ženska v sivem šalu in pletla. Ni dvignila pogleda.

**Orem**  
Bila je četrta noč. Dimnik je zapel, nato pa je bila ulica oranžna. Spominjam se zvoka žlice v praznem loncu. Spominjam se pletilk, ki so ležale v pepelu.

**Edda**  
Dober večer, Orem. Še tri dni do tega, kajne?

**Orem**  
Tri, potem četrta noč. Edda. Žal mi je, da se te spominjam tako.

**Edda**  
Saj sedim tukaj. Pazi na svoje čase.

Za Illuminaro je prišel moški širokih ramen, z mojstrskimi brazgotinami od opeklin na obeh podlahteh, za njim pa sta dva vajenca držala ročni voziček kakor par živčnih nosačev krste. Inge Voss, ki je dvaindvajset let vodila Karrowski ceh hladilnih peči, je gledala bitje, ne tujke.

**Inge Voss**  
Leto tega bi še prenesla. Prejšnji teden se je naučilo številk. Velika talina se začne četrto noč, moji steklarji pa so se začeli spraševati, ob kateri uri bo požar. To se mora končati. Voziček gre nocoj na pot proti kamnolomu.

**Illuminara**  
Mojstrica Voss. Kaj pravi takega, na kar ne morete odgovoriti?

**Inge Voss**  
Prav v tem je težava. Če je njegov jutri dejstvo, ne morem storiti ničesar, zaradi dejstva pa ne bom ustavila celoletnega dela. Če ni dejstvo, zakaj potem tujec kriči na mojem trgu?
To je bil dober ugovor in Illuminara je opazila, da jo je razveselil. Mesto, ki bi se bitju le posmehovalo, bi bilo lažje prepričevati in težje pomagati.

**Illuminara**  
Dajte mi čas, dokler svetilke ne ugasnejo. Če se vrnem samo z govorom, vzemite voziček.

**Inge Voss**  
Dokler svetilke ne ugasnejo. Potem voziček.

scenes.title: Minuta prej
paragraphs: *Karrow, Trg svetilk · noč, prvi dan*

Ni začela s požarom. *Počasi,* si je rekla. *Počasno je le zato, ker nihče ni bil pripravljen čakati.* Sedla je na rob vodnjaka na drugi strani od Edde, z dolgo senco bitja čez kolena, in vprašala, kako je biti ono.

**Orem**  
Nihče ni vprašal. ... Kot bi stal na oddaljenem bregu jezera. Voda je svet. Jaz ga vidim z druge strani. Kar je pred vami, je za menoj. Razumeš?

**Illuminara**  
Še ne. Rada bi.

Bitje ji je to razlagalo eno uro, vsak stavek je prispel cel in malo prepozno, ona pa je pustila, da se vsak konča. Nekje v drugi uri je spoznala, da ne čaka več na odgovor. Poslušala je zvok uma, ki je bil leto dni sam z isto žalostjo, žalost pa je imela obliko in ritem, kakor plima.

**Illuminara**  
Povej mi minuto, preden ulica postane oranžna. Potem minuto pred tem.

**Orem**  
Dimnik zapoje. Nizek, votel ton. Žlica v praznem loncu. ... Pred tem modrina. Modrina ob vznožju dimnika, kjer podnevi ni nič modrega. Pred tem vonj v tretji hali. Mastno olje, ki gori. Ne vem, zakaj je vonj tam. Pred tem svetilka na mostu pri zapornici, zelena. Boben dimnika je hladen, Edda pa sedi v tretji hali s svojo čutaro in reče: No, to pa ni prav.

**Edda**  
To bi rekla, da veš. Natanko to bi rekla.

**Illuminara**  
Orem. Je to, česar se spominjaš, razsodba ali zemljevid?
Bitje je obmirovalo. V svetlobi svetilk se je steklo njegovega obraza počasi zameglilo, kakor ko misel potuje skozi globoko vodo.

**Orem**  
Ne vem. Nihče mi ni nikoli rekel, da se lahko motim. ... Če me pripraviš do zmote, bom izgubil pepel. Izgubil bom njen obraz v njem. Tako skrbno sem ga hranil.

**Edda**  
Ne bodi mevžast. Obdržal boš obraz, ki ga imam.
Illuminara mu ni rekla, da ne bo bolelo. Dlan je položila na hladni rob med njima, kjer je bil kamen še topel od dneva, in jo pustila tam.

**Illuminara**  
Rada bi bila razlog, da se motiš. Ne bom spremenila ničesar tvojega. Spremenila bom le stvari v svetu in te vprašala, kaj najdeš. Smem?

**Orem**  
Da. ... Da. Raje bi se motil, kakor da bi to obdržal.

scenes.title: Trije listki
paragraphs: *Karrow, mojstričino dvorišče · jutro, drugi dan*
Voss je prišla s prekrižanimi rokami in prinesla kapo, polno papirja. Izpraznila jo je na nakovalo in jasno je bilo, da je bila budna prav tako dolgo kot Illuminara.

**Inge Voss**  
Ne bom dovolila, da moje dvorišče prepriča tujka, ki se strinja z vsem, kar pravi to bitje. Tri stvari, ki jih človek lahko spremeni v eni uri. Zapisala sem jih in tudi novo stanje vsake. Niste jih videli. Storili boste tisto, kar izžrebam. Njemu ne bomo povedali ničesar, Edda pa bo sedela na njem kakor koklja, dokler ne končate.

**Illuminara**  
Dobro. Če bi izbrala jaz, bi lahko rekli, da je Orem to prebral z mojega obraza.

**Inge Voss**  
To lahko še vedno rečem. Žrebajte.
Iz kape je izvlekla en listek, ga štirikrat prepognila in ga podala Illuminari, ne da bi za trenutek izpustila vogal. Illuminara ga je enkrat prebrala.
*Zamenjaj dimniško steklo tretje svetilke na mostu pri zapornici z jantarnim.*

Druga dva listka je Voss obdržala: na enem je pisalo, naj mostno zapornico obrnejo navzven, na drugem, naj na vzhodni steber obesijo zvonec. Spravila ju je v predpasnik, kjer ju ni bilo mogoče obtožiti.

**Illuminara**  
Mojstrica Voss, še nekaj. Če se bo izkazalo, da se moti, bo to povedal.

**Inge Voss**  
Svetilka je, ženska. Imel bo prav ali pa ne.

Do poldneva je bilo jantarno steklo v železni kletki na mostu pri zapornici in prvič po letu dni je stara svetilka nad vodo gorela v barvi čaja. Illuminara je šla nazaj skozi trg in ni pogledala proti trgu.

scenes.title: Kaj je povedalo
paragraphs: *Karrow, Trg svetilk · mrak, drugi dan*
Vprašali so ga ob prižiganju svetilk, Voss je stala tri korake zadaj, poleg nje pa zidar Dov Haldane. Dova so poklicali za pričo, ker ni zaupal ničemur in se ni niti enkrat zlagal o zidu.

**Inge Voss**  
Orem. Četrta noč. Povej mi o svetilki na mostu pri zapornici. Potem o zapornici. Potem o zvoncu.

**Orem**  
Svetilka je jantarna. ... Včeraj je bila zelena. Zelene se zelo dobro spominjam, ker jo gledam že leto dni. Zdaj je jantarna, ne vem zakaj in tega nisem izbral. Zapornica je kakor prej. Zvonec je kakor prej.
Nihče ni spregovoril. Edda je odložila pletilke.

**Orem**  
Požara se ne spominjam nič drugače. Dimnik zapoje. Ulica je oranžna. Toda svetilka je jantarna. Z mojim jutri je nekaj narobe, in narobe je natanko tam, kjer je bila ona.
Illuminara ni čutila zmagoslavja. Bolj je bilo podobno temu, da zelo dolgo držiš iztegnjeno roko in naposled začutiš, da nekdo okrog nje sklene prste.

**Dov Haldane**  
Ena možnost od treh, da je po sreči uganil pravi listek, jantarna pa je ena barva od šestih, torej recimo ena od osemnajstih. Na sejmu sem videl večjo srečo. Trik z dobro vestjo.

**Inge Voss**  
Pošteno, Dov. Ena svetilka dokazuje, da vidi svetilko. Ne dokazuje dimnika.

**Illuminara**  
Se strinjam. Svetilka je poceni del spomina. Mojstrica Voss, nocoj bi rada spremenila več poceni delov, listke pa naj izžreba vaš vajenec. Iščem drage dele.

**Dov Haldane**  
Potem naredite tako, da mu lahko spodleti. Petnajst sprememb. Voss nocoj, še pred prvim vprašanjem, zapiše vsak predmet in njegovo novo stanje, jaz pa seznam zapečatim. Šest stvari pustimo pri miru in ga vseeno vprašamo po njih, pomešane med druge; tako ne bo mogel za vse reči, da je spremenjeno. Če zgreši dve ali nespremenjeno stvar označi kot spremenjeno, je zemljevid le zgodba.

**Inge Voss**  
Potem gre voziček. In poslušajte: talina je na temperaturi in ulivanje teče po uri. Ne bom ga zadržala zaradi vas ali zaradi požara. Če odprete moj dimnik, ga boste odprli, medtem ko pesek teče.

**Illuminara**  
Velja, oboje. Če spremenim petnajst majhnih stvari in mi pri vseh sledi, šest nedotaknjenih pa ostane takih kot prej, potem svetilka, zapornica in zvonec nikoli niso bili tisto, iz česar je nastal požar. In karkoli se ne pusti spremeniti—

**Dov Haldane**  
—je tisto, iz česar je nastal požar. Ja. To je zemljevid delov, ki štejejo.
Izrekel je brez topline in s tako očitnim poklicnim zanimanjem, da ga je Voss ostro pogledala. Nato je poslala po vajenca.

scenes.title: Česar ni bilo mogoče premakniti
paragraphs: *Karrow, Trg svetilk · noč, drugi dan*

Do polnoči je bilo petnajst od petnajstih in šest od šestih pri stvareh, ki se jih nihče ni dotaknil. Vajenec Wil je z jezikom med zobmi vlekel listke iz Dovove zapečatene kape: moder trak na vodnjaku, štruca na stopnici pri zapornici, vrata na vzhodnem stebru pobarvana belo. Orem je vsako spremembo imenoval takoj, ko so ga vprašali, ne da bi pogledal, in vsakič je bila sprememba natanko tam, kjer je pisalo z Vossinim črnilom. Voss ni več govorila ena od osemnajstih.

**Dov Haldane**  
Pekov znak.

**Orem**  
Kakor prej. ... Poskušate me ujeti, mojster Haldane.

**Dov Haldane**  
Ja.
Zvenel je malce razočarano. Druga stvar pa se ni premaknila. Edda jim jo je preštela na prste.

**Edda**  
Dimnik zapoje. Modrina ob vznožju. Olje v tretji hali. Jaz v tretji hali, ko rečem, da nekaj ni prav. Štiri. Za vse vaše trakove se ne premakne niti za prst.

**Illuminara**  
Ker se trakovi niso nikoli dotaknili vzroka. Orem, ton dimnika. Kako visoko in na kateri strani?

**Orem**  
Na strani, od koder veter ne piha. Dva razpona visoko. Kjer dimnik tretje hale vstopi v veliki dimnik. Ton ni v opeki. Za njo je.

**Dov Haldane**  
Za njo. To je votla obloga. Votlina za obložno opeko, hladen dimnik pa je še vedno videti krasen. In kjer se dimnik tretje hale priključi velikemu, je železen obroč, ki ga je stari Haakon vgradil po poplavi. Železo in opeka se segrevata različno hitro. Obloga poči tam, kjer nihče ne vidi; razpoka v oblogi vleče zrak v napačno smer, vlek se obrne nazaj v halo, kjer gori oljenka.

**Edda**  
Povratni vlek. To je vonj po masti. Zato diši po kuhinji.

Illuminara je ob eni zjutraj šla k dimniku in nanj položila obe dlani. Teža je ležala skozi opeko tako, kot je ležala devetdeset let, povsem običajno, povsem tiho. Čutila je težo obroča in nič drugega. Razpoka, ki se odpre le v vročini, v hladnem zidu nima sile, in dolgo je stala z rokami na kamnu, jezna nase, nato pa ne več jezna.

**Illuminara**  
Ne najdem je. Ne v hladnem. Zdaj vam lahko povem, kje iskati, ker mi je povedalo jezero. Ne morem pa vam povedati, da je tam.

**Dov Haldane**  
Jaz lahko. S palico. Ob prvem svitu.

scenes.title: Palica
paragraphs: *Karrow, veliki dimnik · zora, tretji dan*
Voss je vztrajala, da bo potrkala sama, in preden je vzela palico, je to povedala vsem na dvorišču, da pozneje nihče ne bi mogel trditi, kaj je mislila.

**Inge Voss**  
Če zazveni, voziček odpelje tujko in njeno svetilko, ulivanje pa gre po načrtu. Če je votlo, znižam ogenj pod talino in odpremo dimnik.

**Dov Haldane**  
Znižate ogenj? Najboljša nočna talina bo šla v nič, šest stotov premoga pa z njo. Hladilna peč ne bo vlekla, dokler se masa ne strdi.

**Inge Voss**  
Ja. In ne boste udarjali s kladivom po zidu, ko je na drugi strani talina na polni temperaturi. To je vaše pravilo, Dov. Kdo plača, je moje.

Vzela je Dovovo jekleno palico, tanko stvar z gumijastim nastavkom, se po zavetrni strani povzpela na oder, medtem ko je od spodaj gledalo vse dvorišče, palica pa je po zdravi opeki zazvenela svetlo kakor zvonec. Dva razpona višje se je ustavila. Znova je potrkala.
Ni zazvenelo. Zaslišalo se je kakor žlica v praznem loncu.
Nekaj časa se ni premaknila. Ko je prišla dol, je bil njen obraz siv kakor stara žlindra.

**Inge Voss**  
Votlo je. Za čelno plastjo je votlina širine dlani, vse okrog obroča. Dvaindvajset let kurim ta dimnik.

**Dov Haldane**  
Tudi jaz. Niti enkrat ga nisva hladnega udarila tam.

Voss se je obrnila in poslala fanta teč proti talilnici. Ko je bil oder postavljen, so ognji v njej potonili v rdeč spanec, steklo v loncu pa se je začelo strjevati in motneti, najboljša nočna talina je odtekala v izgubo.

**Inge Voss**  
Rekla sem, da zaradi požara ne bom zadržala ulivanja. Ne zadržujem ga zaradi požara. Zadržujem ga zaradi zidarja. Ponovno ga bom obložila, Dov. Ker zidar pravi, da je slab. Ne zato, ker tako pravita tujka in svetilka. Razumemo?

**Dov Haldane**  
Isti zid, Inge.

**Inge Voss**  
Isti zid.

Dovova ekipa je do popoldneva izrezala obroč. Illuminara je na odru prevzela njegovo težo, tri tone starega železa je dvignila za prst nad opeko, da so lahko zidarji odstranili počeno oblogo, ne da bi jo udarec kladiva podrl. Držala ga je šest minut in Edda ji je merila čas. Odložila ga je, ko je Dov rekel zdaj, niti trenutek prej, nato pa je šla z odra s tresočimi podlahtmi, ker je bil to Dovov zid.

Delali so vso noč tretjega dne in naprej v četrtega, pod reflektorji in s hitro vezočo maso, opoldne pa se je talilnica prebudila na svežem premogu. Voss je vsakemu zidarju plačala dvojno in nikoli ni povedala zakaj.

scenes.title: Eddine pletilke
paragraphs: *Karrow, Trg svetilk · večer, peti dan*

Velika talina se je začela četrto noč, ulivanje ob mraku, hladilna peč je vlekla lepo in enakomerno, enajsti zvon pa je prišel in minil nad četrtjo nizkih streh in tihih dimnikov. Nihče ni vzkliknil. Karrow je stal na pragovih in poslušal veter, nato pa so ljudje drug za drugim odšli spat, kakor ljudje storijo, kadar se nekaj ni zgodilo.

Peti večer se je Illuminara vrnila k vodnjaku. Edda je sedela na svojem mestu s pletilkami, bitje pa na robu, obraz obrnjen proti jantarni svetilki na mostu pri zapornici, ki je bila še vedno edina svetilka v četrti v barvi čaja.

**Orem**  
Vprašali so me, česa se spominjam o četrti noči. ... Tiho je. Dimnik ne poje. Spiš, Edda, v škornjih, svetilka pa je jantarna. Pepela nimam več. Poskušal sem ga obdržati. Ugotavljam, da ga ne morem.

**Edda**  
No, glej no.

**Orem**  
Nisem vedel, da mi bo tako žal, ko ga izgubim. Hranil sem ga eno leto. Bil je zadnji kraj, kjer sem imel njen obraz.
Illuminara je to začutila in dovolila, da ostane začuteno. Ni rekla, da je cena majhna. Bitje se je odpovedalo letu žalosti, leto pa ni bilo majhno.

**Illuminara**  
Ne morem obljubiti, da je njen obraz še kje drugje kakor v pepelu. Toda osem palcev od tvojega komolca je. Bi jo rad pogledal? Lahko rečeš ne.

**Orem**  
... Da.
Dolga glava se je obrnila. Svetloba svetilk je prispela pozno in se ustalila na sivem šalu, rokah in napeti volni.

**Orem**  
Plete. Rokav. Izpustila je petljo in se pretvarja, da je ni. ... Brunda ton, ki je prenizek.

**Edda**  
Ni prenizek.

**Orem**  
Malo je prenizek. Rad bi ga slišal jutri.

Inge Voss je prišla čez trg, ko so svetilke pobirale zadnjo svetlobo, široka postava z zavihanimi rokavi in knjigo pod roko. Illuminare ni pogledala. Ni se opravičila in nihče v Karrowu ni pričakoval, da se bo. Knjigo je odprla na robu vodnjaka ob bitju in jo obrnila tako, da jo je lahko prebralo.

**Inge Voss**  
Ceh je glasoval. Od naslednjega kurjenja naprej vsak dimnik potrkamo hladnega, preden ga prižgemo, trkanje pa vpišemo v knjigo. Tukaj je prazna vrstica. Nimamo imena za to, kar si tej četrti, in jaz ti ga ne bom dala. Napiši ga sam.

**Orem**  
... Rad bi, da me vprašate, ne da mi ukažete. Povedal bom, česa se spominjam, vsakomur, ki me vpraša, in rekel bom, da se spominjam, ne da se bo zgodilo. Nihče ne ukrepa, dokler zidar ne uporabi palice. In lahko sem tiho. Nekaj tega, česar se spominjam, je Eddino.

**Dov Haldane**  
To je moje pravilo, bitje. Z veseljem.

**Inge Voss**  
Zapisano. In kaj želiš od nas?

**Orem**  
Ne vem, kaj je običajno. ... Stolček pri vodnjaku, ki je že moj. Jantarno svetilko pustite tako. In da nekdo v knjigo zapiše vsakič, ko se motim. Rad bi se motil pisno.

**Inge Voss**  
Svetilka ostane. Wil vodi knjigo, za to ima roko. Čaj je še vedno neobvezen.

**Orem**  
Ne pijem čaja.

**Inge Voss**  
Rekla sem neobvezen.
Šla je nazaj čez trg in se ni obrnila. Edda je stisnila pletilke skupaj in začela novo vrsto.

**Orem**  
Edda. Nečesa se spominjam. Prva slana. Čez tri tedne. Daleč je in samo slana je. Povem tebi, ne cehu. ... Ne vem, ali je res.

**Edda**  
Potem bova šla pogledat, kajne.

translation_sl.critic_line: Opozorilo žalovalca iz počasnega stekla postane preverljiv, svobodno skupen reševalni načrt, ne pa prerokba, vsiljena od zgoraj: Dov zagotovi ovrgljive kontrole, Voss plača odprtje nevarnega dimnika, Orem izbere vzajemne pogoje za svoj dar, delavci pri pečeh pa ohranijo pristojnost, s katero preprečijo požar.
